Subject: Uploads failing after private cutover — intermittent timeouts and resets

Vanessa,

We cut traffic over to the private VPC path at 10:00 PDT and immediately started seeing intermittent failures from our ingest workers to Redwood's private ingress (POST /v1/uploads). Approx 15% of requests time out or return TCP RST. Same clients are able to retry successfully against the hosted public endpoints.

Attached I’m sending a sample pcap of one failed upload and the curl trace from our side. Not sure if this is an MTU/fragmentation problem or something on the return path — we see truncated packets and occasional ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages in the capture.

Can you confirm which route table and security group set we should be using for the private cutover?

Thanks,
Alan

Quick checks for Kernel Labs team while we triage:

Marissa & Karthik — I’m adding you both. I’ve attached the pcap to this thread. Assigning INF-4721.

Subject: Re: Uploads failing after private cutover — initial triage notes

Alan/Vanessa,

I pulled the pcap and correlated it with our ingress logs. Key observations so far (preliminary):
- The client SYN arrives at our edge and we reply with SYN-ACK. In several cases the client re-sends SYN or we see RSTs after a small data burst.
- There are ICMPv4 "Fragmentation Needed" messages originating from an intermediate hop (ASN translated) back to the client, indicating MTU path discovery issues.
- For a subset of flows, the server-side (our) egress to Kernel Labs goes out via a different private egress (private-backup-route) that has a lower priority in the table but _advertises_ via a different BGP next-hop. That creates asymmetric return path and ephemeral port mapping issues on their NAT.
- Our security group for the private-path ingress is permissive for TCP 443 but we do not have an explicit ephemeral port egress allow policy documented for the private tenant link — the default implicit-deny on the egress ACL on the partner-facing firewall could be dropping the return.

Immediate mitigations I propose:
1) For short-term relief, bump the route priority for the primary private path so our SR-encoded flows egress via the same next-hop (reduce flapping to backup route).
2) Add explicit egress rules on the partner-facing SG to allow ephemeral ports 32768-61000 transiently for Kernel Labs (tighten to only their source CIDRs).
3) Recommend enabling MSS clamping on the on-prem and our edge to prevent large segmented packets requiring fragmentation. I’ll prepare the playbook.

I’m attaching a small diff of route tables and a first-pass MSS clamp playbook.

-M

--
Marissa Cole
Network SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alan Reynolds <alan@kernellabs.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Jul 2028 01:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uploads failing after private cutover — action plan

Thanks Marissa — I executed a staged change at 00:45 PDT:
- Adjusted route table priority so primary-private-path has a higher route propagation metric (primary now preferred). Change validated with traceroute and BGP next-hop table.
- Temporary egress SG rule added for Kernel Labs CIDRs to allow 32768-61000 from our private-egress (rule expires after 6 hours).
- Enabled MSS clamp of 1380 on the fence (both sides) to minimize fragmentation; this is a non-disruptive TCP stack change.

Monitoring notes: since 00:55 PDT we see a drop in failures from ~15% to <1% on kernel uploads for the test fleet. No RST storms observed in the captures collected post-change.

Next steps:
- Confirm Kernel Labs sees stable uploads for 24 hours.
- Work with Kernel Labs to validate their on-prem NAT and ensure symmetric routing on their side for the permanent cutover.
- Schedule a post-mortem and update INF-4721 with root cause and permanent config changes (route metrics + SG policy + MSS clamp as needed).

Karthik
